question: For a basic rural roadside sign, combine Figure 2A-2 with Sections 2A.15 and 2A.16 to state the normal minimum mounting height and lateral offset.
model_answer: Direct Answer: For a basic roadside sign in a rural area, the normal minimum mounting height is 5 feet, measured vertically from the bottom of the sign to the elevation of the near edge of the pavement. The normal minimum lateral offset shown in Figure 2A-2 is 12 feet from the edge of the traveled way, or 6 feet from the edge of the shoulder where the shoulder is wider than 6 feet. Where terrain or vegetation make these offsets impractical, a reduced offset of at least 2 feet is permitted on certain roads. Standards (mandatory): - "In rural areas, the minimum height, measured vertically from the bottom of the sign to the elevation of the near edge of the pavement, of signs installed at the side of the road shall be 5 feet (see Figure 2A-2)." - For contrast, in business, commercial, or residential areas where parking, bicyclist, or pedestrian movements are likely, "the minimum height... of signs installed at the side of the road shall be 7 feet (see Figure 2A-2)." - "Where signs serve both bicyclists and other road users, vertical mounting height and lateral placement shall be as provided in Sections 2A.15 and 2A.16 of this manual." Guidance (recommended): - The figure notes accompanying Section 2A.13 explain that "Lateral offset is a minimum of 6 feet measured from the edge of the shoulder, or 12 feet measured from the edge of the traveled way," and refer to Section 2A.16 for reduced lateral offsets where space is limited. Options (permitted): - "On conventional, low-volume rural, and special-purpose roads in areas where it is impractical to locate a sign with the lateral offset prescribed by this Section because of roadside features such as terrain or vegetation, a lateral offset of at least 2 feet may be used." Visual evidence: [Image 1] Figure 2A-2 diagram A ("Roadside sign in rural area") shows a STOP sign with "12 ft MIN." lateral offset from the traveled way and "5 ft MIN." mounting height, while diagram B shows a "6 ft MIN." offset from the edge of a shoulder wider than 6 feet with the same "5 ft MIN." height. [Image 2] Figure 2A-2 on page 51 repeats these dimensions and includes the note referring to Section 2A.16 for reduced lateral offsets. [Image 4] The Section 2A.15 text confirms the mounting height standards and states that "Figure 2A-2 illustrates some examples of the mounting height requirements contained in this Section," and begins Section 2A.16 Lateral Offset. [Image 5] Figure 2A-3 confirms the note that "Lateral offset is a minimum of 6 feet measured from the edge of the shoulder, or 12 feet measured from the edge of the traveled way." [Image 3] Figure 2M-3 (recreational areas) similarly shows 12 ft minimum offset and 5 ft minimum height for a rural roadside assembly, consistent with the rural pattern. Citations: - Section 2A.15 Standard §4 (p.58) - Section 2A.15 Standard §5 (p.58) - Section 9A.02 Standard §4 (p.1047) - Section 2A.13 Guidance §6 (p.57) - Section 2A.16 Option §9 (p.60) - Figure 2A-2 (p.51) - Page 92 - Page 100 - Page 93
gold_answer: The minimum mounting height is 5 feet. The normal minimum lateral offset is 12 feet from the edge of the traveled way, or 6 feet from the edge of a shoulder wider than 6 feet.
